theme: GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC against bnlearn on the papers' networks and on linear-Gaussian graphs, every node a target
build: GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: Andrey pre-release build of 12 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch with gs, fast_iamb, and hiton_pc as merged)
verdict_rule: GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: per cell (network or Gaussian graph, rows; 20 datasets, every node a target): per dataset, the mean over the targets with a nonempty true set of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1) (an empty answer counts precision 1, distance 1) and of the set's F1; D = Andrey's minus bnlearn's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 was not rerun
fit_protocol: GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, every node of a dataset a target in one fit, no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored
error_metric: GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: set_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1); set_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of the set's F1. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members (the wrong answers of andrey.metrics.target_answer_scores), against the empty set's, the true set's size
complete_definition: GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: true when every row has at least 10 paired datasets (both fitted)
seeds_note: GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; a rerun holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39

regimes.discrete: net:<network>:<rows>: forward samples of the bnlearn repository network, columns that hold one value dropped with their nodes
regimes.gaussian: gauss:<d>:<rows>[:<mean degree>]: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graph, standardized, mean degree 2 unless given

hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; Andrey and bnlearn ran in the same run, one fit after the other, on shared nodes

methods.setting: alpha=0.05, max_depth=None (the default), G-square on categorical data and Fisher's z on continuous data
